transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Alex Reyes (Quantaco PM), Priya Nair (Quantaco Infra), Sam Okoro (Quantaco ML)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC cost/unit economics, review of tokens/sec/$ numbers from last week's bench, discussion of caching savings and batching tradeoffs, and agreement on next steps (send spreadsheet, share raw logs, schedule deep-dive). Some audio artifacts; speaker labelling may jump.

Topics:
- Current throughput numbers and cost per 1M tokens
- Impact of prefix/KV caching on token cost and latency
- Batching tradeoffs: latency vs tokens/sec/$
- Dedicated vs hosted pricing sensitivity
- Action items and timeline for pilot phase end

Action items (recap):
- Maya: updated cost model spreadsheet
- Diego: caching & batch logs
- Priya: traffic histogram

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call, and then we'll dive into the cost numbers - we got the benchmarking back from last week.
00:18 Alex: Yep, I'm here, Priya and Sam are on as well.
00:25 Diego: Quick note, some of the traces have slightly off timestamps, so you'll see a couple of offsets in the logs.
00:33 Priya: that's fine. go ahead.
00:37 Maya: Ok so high-level — we ran the open-llm variant on a dedicated pool and on hosted for the same workloads. The headline: tokens per second improved ~1.8x on Dedicated with our batching profile, cost per 1M tokens dropped ~22% due to caching and batching combo.
01:02 Sam: can you say the baseline latency numbers again? we saw some spikes.
01:08 Diego: Baseline (no cache, small batches) tail p95 was ~420ms, average ~230ms. With continuous KV cache enabled and moderate batching (batch size ~8) p95 moved to ~520ms on some requests, but tokens/sec jumped from ~900 to ~1,600. so throughput improved but latency tradeoff obvious.
01:40 Alex: So tokens/sec per dollar — what's the delta hosted vs dedicated?
01:44 Maya: Hosted (our current hosted catalog model) is about X tokens/sec/$ — for privacy I'll just say hosted yields 0.9 relative units while Dedicated gives you 1.8 relative units for quantized fp16 variant. dollar-per-token was 22% lower on Dedicated for that workload.
02:05 Priya: Are those numbers accounting for prefix caching? because our workload is highly repetitive — lots of shared prompts.
02:12 Diego: yes — caching accounted for roughly 35% of token savings in this workload. prefix/KV cache prevented regen of first ~40 tokens on many requests. Note: the autocache heuristics sometimes mis-detect on very noisy prompts — saw a few misses.
02:36 Sam: hmm, those misses — are they due to punctuation differences or tokenization variances?
02:40 Diego: mostly tokenization and small paraphrase differences. We can tune TTL and the similarity threshold; that'll increase cache hit rate but at potential staleness cost.
02:54 Alex: From a product POV our biggest concern is latency for interactive flows. Even if tokens/sec/$ is better, can't degrade UX.
03:02 Maya: totally — that's why the tradeoff matrix matters. For batch inference (report gen) we favor higher batching and cache use; for interactive, we keep batch small and rely on prefix caching only. Also Redwood has fallback lanes — if p95 latency crosses SLO we route to a lower-latency variant, albeit at higher cost.
03:27 Priya: what's the cost delta if we enable stricter caching thresholds — do we risk more stale outputs and more cache misses needing fallback?
03:34 Diego: stricter thresholds (higher similarity) reduce hits but improve quality; the cost delta was about +3-5% in overall token spend because we miss some cheap cached tokens but avoid repeated low-quality cached output re-runs.
03:50 Sam: can you walk through an example? like request A where cache helps and request B where it hurts.
03:55 Diego: Sure — request A: user prompt has long stable prefix, cache returns first 40 tokens saved, we only generate 120 tokens new -> big savings. Request B: user changes small part of prompt, cache mismatch returns, we regenerate full 160 tokens and extra compute for the mismatch so net no saving and slight latency increase.
04:25 Alex: About batching — you mentioned batch size 8. what's the latency delta if we go to batch 16?
04:31 Diego: average latency goes up ~30-40ms per request, but tokens/sec improves another ~20-25% on our GPUs. For many backend flows that trade is worth it; for UI interactive it isn't.
04:44 Priya: I want to flag our peak traffic — we have 12k concurrent chats in the peak hour. need to map how that maps to batching windows.
04:53 Maya: got it, Priya — that's why we asked for your traffic histogram. Diego, we might need to carve a hybrid routing policy here.
05:02 Diego: Exactly. We can route interactive traffic to a low-latency pool (small batch, high cost) and background/async jobs to a high-throughput pool.
05:12 Alex: Can the same model binary be used in both pools? worried about consistency and model drift.
05:16 Diego: yes, same model versions; quantization profile may differ slightly (e.g., 8-bit on high-throughput pool vs fp16 on low-latency), but Redwood supports variant mapping and automatic fallback if quality regression crosses threshold.
05:32 Priya: security question — for Dedicated we need KMS integration and audit logs. Are those included in the POC?
05:38 Maya: Dedicated includes KMS integration, HSM option for Private, and we can push audit logs to your SIEM during the pilot. We'll send the SOC2/ISO checklist again.
05:49 Alex: also curious about data residency — some EU tenants require tokens to never leave region. how's that handled?
05:55 Diego: routing by region is supported; we pin requests to region-local pools. There was a small mislabel in last week's logs where a few test requests were routed via us-east due to metadata config, we'll correct that.
06:14 Sam: about quantization — we're seeing small regressions in hallucination in 8-bit on longer context, is that expected?
06:20 Diego: There can be, yes. Our recommendation was to keep fp16 for critical path and 8-bit for high throughput non-sensitive outputs. Also we can fine-tune calibration and kernel selection to reduce regression.
06:33 Alex: Pricing ask — can we see host vs dedicated line items broken down: compute, caching savings, network egress, and support?
06:40 Maya: yes, that's the sheet I'm updating — will break down tokens, compute hours, reserved capacity vs burst, and expected monthly costs at your traffic profile.
06:49 Priya: For the caching logs Diego will need to share raw traces — how big are those? can we get s3 links?
06:55 Diego: It's about 1.2GB compressed for the last week; I'll upload and share link with ACL to Quantaco infra.
07:05 Alex: ok good. Next, what's the expected unit economics if we assume a 40% cache hit rate and prebatching to size 8?
07:12 Diego: Roughly tokens/$ improves by ~30% compared to baseline. If you push hit rate to 60% by tuning similarity and TTL you'll see closer to 45% improvement.
07:24 Sam: any risks of cache poisoning or stale prompts leaking sensitive data?
07:29 Diego: cache is encrypted at rest and in transit, we scrub PII heuristically before caching; but for strict compliance you can opt-out of caching for designated routes.
07:41 Priya: we'll probably opt-out for auth flows.
07:44 Maya: makes sense.
07:46 Alex: Also can we get a quick SLAs summary for Dedicated?
07:50 Maya: Dedicated has an SLA commitment on uptime and latency tiers; I'll attach the SLA doc. For pilot we run without full SLA but with monitoring hooks.
08:02 Priya: technical: does Redwood support kernel pinning or specific GPU types? we prefer A100s in our on-prem.
08:09 Diego: yes we support GPU family pinning and kernel selection; in Dedicated you can request a particular instance type. On-prem we support our private deployment with the same runtime.
08:19 Sam: can you clarify the batching algorithm — is it fixed-window or lateness-based?
08:23 Diego: it's a hybrid: continuous batching with max wait threshold, plus priority lanes for interactive. you tune max batch size and latency SLO and runtime adapts.
08:36 Alex: For the next steps, let's confirm dates — we want cost breakdown by Friday and sample logs asap.
08:42 Maya: I'll send spreadsheet by Friday (11/20). Diego will post logs by 11/19. Priya will send traffic histogram by 11/20. We should lock the deep dive for week of 11/23.
08:55 Priya: noted.
09:00 Maya: any other risks we didn't cover?
09:03 Sam: one more: cold start for KV cache when you scale up quickly — we saw a few cold periods.
09:08 Diego: heard — we can pre-warm cache for predictable prefixes during traffic surges; that reduces cold-start cost.
09:15 Alex: great. good call.
09:18 Maya: ok recap and I'll shoot the spreadsheet. Thanks everyone.
09:22 (end)
